data.title: Haze-linked First Resources, Bumitama post higher profits for Q3
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Two palm oil companies linked to the transboundary haze in October reported higher profits for the third quarter ended Sept 30, in separate business updates published on the morning of Nov 13.

Palm oil producer First Resources posted a 40.1% rise in its underlying net profit to US$122.7 million (S$157.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, from US$87.5 million in the year-ago period.

The increase was boosted by higher sales of palm oil products and fruit bunches harvested from oil palms, it said.

Sales were up 24.9% at US$578.6 million for the quarter, compared with US$463.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 26.6% to US$207.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from US$163.8 million a year ago.

For the nine months ended Sept 30, sales grew 36.5% year on year to US$1.6 billion, driven by higher sales volumes.

A net inventory drawdown of 28,000 tonnes over the nine-month period, compared with a build-up of 80,000 tonnes in the corresponding period in 2025, also supported higher sales volumes.

The group’s stronger production output in the first nine months of 2026 was also attributable in part to the full nine-month contribution from Austindo Nusantara Jaya, an Indonesian agribusiness company acquired in May 2025.

However, profits were partially offset by foreign currency translation losses resulting from the depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah against the US dollar.

The group said it expects demand for palm oil to remain supported by Indonesia’s biodiesel programme.

In addition, elevated crude oil prices arising from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are expected to support biodiesel economics and crude palm oil demand.

Performance supported by productivity improvements

Meanwhile, Bumitama reported a 1.9% increase in its net profit to 614.1 billion rupiah (S$43.4 million) for the quarter ended Sept 30, compared with 602.9 billion rupiah in the previous corresponding period.

For the nine-month period, net profit rose 30.6% to 2.4 trillion rupiah, up from 1.9 trillion rupiah in the year-ago period.

Revenue increased 9.7% to 4.2 trillion rupiah in the third quarter, up from 3.9 trillion rupiah a year ago. For the nine-month period, revenue was up 20% at 16.3 trillion rupiah.

Bumitama said its performance was supported by productivity improvements in its plantations and mills, particularly during the earlier part of the quarter.

In July, internal production of fresh fruit bunches reached 383,203 tonnes, accounting for almost 40% of the quarter’s production.

Quarterly production of crude palm oil increased 14% year on year to 368,323 tonnes.

However, exceptionally dry weather conditions in its Kalimantan estates during the third quarter put additional pressure on logistics infrastructure and disrupted shipments, said Bumitama.

Consequently, third-quarter revenue declined compared with the second quarter.

The prolonged dry season also heightened the risk of land and forest fires across parts of Kalimantan.

Fires affected certain areas within or adjoining the group’s concessions, including community-managed, conservation and unplanted land, the group noted.

Bumitama said that elevated energy prices and Indonesia’s biodiesel programme coupled with a relatively constrained palm oil supply growth could provide a “supportive backdrop” for palm oil fundamentals heading into 2027.

However, market conditions remain subject to uncertainty.

These include changes in global energy prices, supply-and-demand dynamics, and the potential effects of prolonged dry weather on future production, it added.

Both First Resources and Bumitama reiterated their commitment to upholding a zero-burning policy, and cooperating with the Indonesian and Singapore authorities in relation to the haze.

Shares of First Resources closed at $2.97, up 6.45%, and those of Bumitama closed flat at $1.39 on Nov 13, after the updates. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Cisco lifts annual revenue forecast on strong AI networking demand
data.description:
Cisco beat Wall Street estimates for first quarter results and raised its annual revenue forecast on Nov 12, as the network gear maker bets on sustained strong demand from companies building out their AI infrastructure.

The company has doubled down on its artificial intelligence efforts through strategic investments as Big Tech’s massive spending moves beyond artificial intelligence processors to the switches and routers required to connect large data centre systems.

Cisco expects fiscal 2027 revenue in the range of US$74.8 billion (S$96.2 billion) to US$75.8 billion, compared with its previous forecast of US$72.2 billion to US73.4 billion.

“We are in the very early stages of a multi-year networking super-cycle,” chief executive Chuck Robbins said in a statement.

The company raised its fiscal 2027 forecast for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to US$9 billion from US$7.5 billion.

The segment generated revenue of US$4 billion a year earlier.

Investors have been worried about a possible slowdown in data centre build-out following Democrats’ sweeping win in the US midterms, as well as rising borrowing costs and their impact on the debt-fuelled construction.

Cisco reported first-quarter revenue of US$18.5 billion, compared with analysts’ average estimate of US$18.14 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company reported an adjusted profit of US$1.40 per share for the quarter ended Oct 24, above estimates of US$1.33.

Cisco is also building software tools that businesses can use to build their own ​armies of bots, known as AI agents, to protect their IT ‌infrastructure against cybersecurity threats.

Shares of the San Jose, California-based company were flat in volatile extended trading.

They have risen about 32% so far in 2026 through the Nov 12 close.

Cisco’s gross margin has been a worry for investors, as a shortage of memory chips has pushed up component costs for hardware makers while suppliers prioritise chips for AI data centre customers.

“A small dip in gross margin is not a major concern given higher memory and component costs,” said Bob O’Donnell, president and chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.

Cisco’s raised annual forecast and results above estimates are what the market wants to see from a company tied to AI infrastructure, he added.

The company reported first quarter adjusted gross margin of 65.6%, in line with estimates, but down from 68.1% a year earlier. REUTERS

data.title: Singapore life insurers pay out more than $15 billion in first nine months of 2026
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Life insurers in Singapore paid out more than $15 billion in insurance claims and maturity benefits in the first nine months of 2026. Policy maturities accounted for the bulk of payouts, followed by claims for healthcare and other forms of insurance protection.

Maturity benefits comprised about 74% of total payouts, or $11.2 billion, while claims under individual health policies amounted to some $2.2 billion, according to figures released by the Life Insurance Association (LIA) Singapore on Nov 12.

Some $1.7 billion was paid out under individual life policies for critical illness, death and total permanent disability. Critical illness claims alone amounted to $756 million.

Of the $2.2 billion in health insurance claims, $2.1 billion came from Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and their riders, with IP riders accounting for 24.1%. The remaining $115.2 million was paid under other medical plans and riders.

Claims under IPs and their riders rose 6.7% quarter on quarter, from $695.1 million in the second quarter to $742 million in the third quarter.

Investment-linked policies gain share

Separately, the industry recorded a 15% year-on-year increase in total weighted new business premiums in the first nine months of 2026 to $5.5 billion, a rise that LIA attributed to strong economic momentum.

In the third quarter alone, weighted new business premiums rose 4.2% year on year to $1.8 billion.

Investment-linked policies (ILPs) accounted for an increasingly large share of new business. New business weighted premiums from ILPs rose 22.6% year on year to $2.5 billion in the first nine months. 

ILPs made up 46% of the industry’s total, up from 43% in the same period a year ago and 37% in 2024.

Their share reached 49.7% in the third quarter, compared with 42.7% in the first quarter and 44.9% in the second quarter.

LIA Singapore president Wong Sze Keed said the growing share of ILPs suggests that consumers are placing a greater emphasis on savings and investment priorities, alongside meeting their protection needs.

“For some, access to professionally managed funds and financial advice may be part of the appeal,” she said.

The industry is working closely with the Monetary Authority of Singapore to strengthen disclosures through product highlight sheets and help customers better understand the overall costs and benefits of ILPs, she added. 

Participating policies also recorded growth, with weighted new business premiums rising 5.7% year on year to $1.2 billion.

These plans provide insurance protection, while policyholders may receive non-guaranteed bonuses or dividends depending on the performance of the insurer’s participating fund.

They accounted for 23% of total weighted new business premiums, down from 25% in 2025.

As at September, about three million people in Singapore were covered by IPs. Including other medical plans and riders, around 3.4 million people were covered by individual health insurance.

Wong said the industry will continue reviewing how insurance responds to evolving healthcare needs and developments in medical care, including through regular reviews of the critical illness framework and how definitions take into account the seriousness of an illness and developments in its treatment.

“This is balanced against the implications for coverage and premiums, with the aim of keeping protection meaningful, affordable and accessible over the long term,” she said. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Nvidia’s next CEO: Some prediction market traders bet Jensen Huang will make a comeback
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Jensen Huang has stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive, but some traders on the prediction market Kalshi are betting that the chipmaker will name him its next permanent CEO before 2029.

Nvidia has yet to name a permanent successor to one of the AI industry’s most influential leaders, with some in the industry calling him irreplaceable.

On Kalshi, which is regulated in the US but banned in Singapore, the implied odds of Nvidia naming Huang as its next permanent chief executive by the end of 2028 rose as high as 15% on the evening of Nov 13, before falling to around 7%.

Nvidia executive Ian Buck is currently in the lead, with a 33% chance on Kalshi of becoming Nvidia’s next CEO.

Buck is vice-president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing at Nvidia. He leads its multibillion-dollar data centre business, which supplies AI chips and software to major tech companies worldwide.

Kalshi put the odds of Colette Kress getting the permanent job at 13%. Kress is Nvidia’s chief financial officer and was made interim CEO following Huang’s resignation on Nov 12.

She is tied with Rene Haas, chief executive of British chip design company Arm Holdings.

Other executives Kalshi traders are betting on include Apple chief hardware officer Johny Srouji, Palo Alto Networks chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora, Nvidia executive vice-president Jay Puri, and AMD chairman and CEO Lisa Su. Puri oversees Nvidia’s global sales, business development and partnerships.

Tech executives, investors and fans have voiced support for Huang, who stepped down following reports of three affairs. He has admitted to being involved with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based, Alibaba-backed data centre firm Megaspeed. She is suspected by the US of spying for China.

“Jensen is one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia Capital, wrote in an X post on Nov 8. He concluded that Nvidia’s Huang is “irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership”.

About an hour later, Elon Musk quoted the post, noting: “I agree.”

Maguire added on Nov 12 that Huang’s ousting “will leave a huge void, with the loss of a technical, aggressive, founder-CEO.

“The American AI community needs to work double-time in an attempt to fill this void.”

Even US President Donald Trump called Huang before he stepped down, urging him to keep fighting for his job, according to The New York Times, quoting sources familiar with the call.

After Huang announced his resignation, Trump wrote in a Nov 12 Truth Social post: “Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – Tim Cook of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”

On prediction market Polymarket, trading implied a 6% chance that Nvidia would name Apple executive chairman Tim Cook as its next permanent chief executive by the end of 2028.

There is also a 11% probability on Polymarket that Nvidia does not find a CEO by Dec 31, 2028.

Regardless of who takes over, Nvidia’s stakes are high because so much of the AI industry relies on chips, delivered by a company that Huang co-founded, transformed and led for the past 30 years.

A total of 60 executives across the firm report directly to him, and there is no succession plan.

Huang’s departure therefore leaves Nvidia investors weighing several risks, Saxo UK investor strategist Neil Wilson said in a Nov 13 note.

Nvidia is “about to find out whether Huang’s grip on the company and flat organisational structure was effectively storing up trouble”, said Wilson.

While a successor could keep Nvidia on the same course, Huang’s detailed knowledge of its products and his hands-on management style is unique and would be hard to replicate.

Wilson also pointed to scrutiny in Washington, citing reported US Justice Department inquiries involving Megaspeed and Alice Huang, and a request by three House committee chairs for a closed-door briefing on Nov 18 over national security concerns.

He expects Nvidia’s relationship with Washington to become more difficult, even with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s support.

Investors, however, appear to think otherwise. Shares of Nvidia, which had fallen from around US$200 to a low of US$150 at the time of Huang’s ousting on Nov 12, have since rebounded and last traded at around US$162 each.

Brokers said trading in Nvidia surged after Huang’s resignation.

According to The Business Times, Nvidia orders at Syfe hit 13 times their six-week daily average in Singapore, while volume at FSM Global reached 11 times its October daily average. At IG, trading volume among Singapore clients rose nearly sixfold from the previous week.

Nvidia still has an edge after Huang’s departure. Its chips are powerful, many developers already use its software to build and run AI models, and it has longstanding ties with major customers.

Still, the lack of a credible succession plan could force Nvidia’s board, and investors, to reassess how much of the company’s future depends on Huang personally.

“He cannot be replaced, but a great CEO can also be found and take the company in a similar direction,” said Wilson. 

For now, at least some traders on Kalshi are betting that Nvidia will turn to Huang again.

data.title: Applied Materials forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates on strong AI chip demand
data.description:
Applied Materials forecast fiscal first-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations on Nov 12, betting that strong demand for advanced AI chips will continue to fuel spending on its semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

The company, which supplies equipment for key wafer fabrication processes, is benefiting from increased spending by chipmakers racing to meet the extraordinary artificial intelligence-led demand for chips and memory.

Shares of the company were marginally higher in extended trading. The stock has risen about 48% in 2026.

“The actual metrics of the market show that demand is still very strong,” said Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.

Applied’s results show chipmakers and foundries are “buying as much equipment as they possibly can”, he added.

The Santa Clara, California-based company’s Semiconductor Systems revenue jumped to US$8 billion (S$10.3 billion) in the fourth quarter, up about 64% from a year earlier.

The company is one of Apple’s partners for its American Manufacturing Program, which includes work at Applied’s Austin, Texas, facility to boost US production of chipmaking equipment.

“We expect 2027 to be another record year for the market and Applied,” chief executive Gary Dickerson said on a post-earnings call.

He said wafer fab equipment demand should rise more than 30% and customers are asking for tools sooner, not later.

China accounted for 25% of fourth-quarter revenue, down from 29% a year earlier, though sales there rose about 35% to US$2.64 billion.

The company forecast quarterly revenue of around US$11.1 billion, plus or minus US$500 million, compared with the average of analysts’ estimates of US$10.89 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company reported fourth-quarter adjusted profit of US$4.16 per share, beating analysts’ average estimate of US$4.05. REUTERS

data.title: Nvidia’s Asian supply chain prepares for life after Jensen Huang
data.description:
TAIPEI/SEOUL – US chip giant Nvidia’s partners and suppliers across Asia, from memory chip powerhouse South Korea to advanced chipmaking hub Taiwan, are redrawing plans in case Chief Executive Jensen Huang is ousted over reports of two extramarital affairs.

Nvidia’s board is meeting late on Nov 11 to decide on Huang’s future, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a sharp shift of tactics from Nov 8, when the board expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team.

“We will support whatever capacity Nvidia needs, but the new CEO may not be as aggressive as Jensen,” said an executive at a Taiwan supplier who feared his company’s expansion could slow if a successor was not as quick to tie up manufacturing capacity.

The executive sought anonymity because the subject is a sensitive one.

Huang has never anointed a successor, but analysts and investors see two candidates as particularly likely, at least for the short term: Nvidia’s uber-engineer Ian Buck and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress.

Any setback for Huang could deprive the AI industry of one of its most vocal champions.

His long-term strategy and direction have turned the chip giant’s swelling cash pile into a war chest to fund companies ranging from AI cloud-computing providers and suppliers to the biggest labs.

“Without him at the helm, we will likely see a slowdown in new, aggressive ecosystem-level investments and lucrative bilateral AI infrastructure deals from NVIDIA side,” said Neil Shah, vice-president of research at Counterpoint Research.

Built strong supplier network during frequent visits

The longtime Nvidia leader has built a strong supplier network in Taiwan during frequent visits to strengthen ties with key manufacturing partners such as TSMC, Foxconn and Wistron.

In May, he said Nvidia planned to invest about US$150 billion (S$192.74 billion) a year in Taiwan.

“He can take technologies his engineers believe are possible and turn them into products the whole company commits resources to, takes risks on, and has to deliver,” said Ming-Chi Kuo, an analyst at TF International Securities.

“That’s why the supply chain gets such strong order visibility and is willing to keep up with aggressive spec upgrades.

“It also forces competitors to follow, which drives technology upgrades and supply chain investment across the entire AI industry.”

Shares in TSMC traded 2% lower, while SK Hynix fell 1.6%. Samsung Electronics rose 0.8%.

TSMC, SK Hynix and Samsung did not immediately respond to requests for comments.

In China, AI companies are seeking to secure overseas access to Nvidia chips, concerned that the scandal could spur Washington to tighten curbs on remote access to advanced processors, Reuters reported on Nov 12.

Companies in South Korea, home to key suppliers of the high-bandwidth memory used in Nvidia’s AI chips, were assessing what a leadership change could mean for their expanding ties with the US firm.

Nvidia and SK Group, parent of memory chipmaker SK Hynix, are pursuing an AI initiative encompassing large-scale data centres and next-generation chips valued at about US$500 billion.

Ties extend beyond chips into robotics

In forging and deepening Nvidia’s ties with South Korean business leaders, Huang has extended partnerships beyond semiconductors into robotics and AI factories.

He personally sketched a roadmap for collaboration on a whiteboard when Lee Hae-jin, founder of South Korean internet firm Naver, visited the US, the latter said.

“We’ve built strong ties with Huang over the years,” said an official at a South Korean chip company with business ties to Nvidia, citing Huang’s accessibility whenever business matters needed to be discussed.

“Our biggest question is whether a potential successor would maintain the same favourable relationship with us.”

Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at Omdia, said Huang’s exit may shift Nvidia’s long-term direction and any slowdown in its execution or loss of clarity over its product roadmap could give rivals more room to catch up.

Still, some investors and analysts expect limited immediate impact from any change of leadership.

“The chips Nvidia will ship over the next year or two are already designed and in production, and its customers’ 2027 spending plans don’t depend on who runs the company,” said Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, which holds Nvidia shares. REUTERS

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end lower as Nvidia uncertainty weighs on tech shares
data.description:
NEW YORK - The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower on Nov 13, as concerns about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

Nvidia’s shares fell 2% and recorded their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday. He stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia’s board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The uncertainty about leadership at the chipmaker has raised concerns about the durability of the AI trade, given Nvidia’s primary role in the industry’s boom and its financial ties to a host of companies in the sector, which has been a pillar of the bull market in equities.

“The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia is going to go through a period of volatility, and you’re going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there’s been a loss of confidence,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan.

“The market and investors are trying to navigate what does the AI theme look like when we have the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia’s balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That’s gone.”

Sweeping Democratic victories in the midterm elections last week also raised concerns about government regulations potentially slowing growth among AI-related companies.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 50.46 points, or 0.10%, to 52,347.55, the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points, or 0.40%, to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 229.82 points, or 0.91%, to 25,136.27.

Despite the recent volatility, the major indexes recorded weekly gains, as the Nasdaq and S&P 500 both snapped a four-week streak of declines. For the week, the S&P 500 gained 2.51%, the Nasdaq rose 2.27% and the Dow climbed 2.07%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4%, with Advanced Micro Devices dropping 8.8% and Broadcom down 4.8% as the biggest drags on the index.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also ended lower, while data center-related firms IREN lost 6.7% and Applied Digital fell 5.8%.

The losses come ahead of AI company Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO next week, which could test investor appetite for established AI heavyweights as money potentially shifts toward the new entrant.

The S&P 500 technology index shed 1.7% and was the worst-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. But Microsoft ended 0.2% higher, as it erased earlier declines after a global outage that included its Outlook and Teams products began to ease.

Airlines dropped in the final minutes of trading with the NYSE Arca airline index closing down 1.4% after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop of all departing flights on Friday. The agency said this was “due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety” after it earlier reported serious air traffic control communications issues.

Inflation concerns remain

On the economic front, the Labor Department said US producer prices were slightly cooler than expected in October, but still shot up 6.5% year over year, the largest annual gain since November 2022.

The data kept expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed’s December meeting completely locked in, with markets pricing in a roughly 10% chance for an outsized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

The sentiment for additional rate hikes was echoed by more Fed officials on Friday, including San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly, who said her “bias” is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, while Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said tighter monetary policy is coming because of high inflation.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.28-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and by a 1.61-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 9 new 52-week highs and 1 new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 37 new highs and 340 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 16.38 billion shares, compared with the 18.52 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days. REUTERS

data.title: Anthropic’s IPO is about six times oversubscribed, say sources
data.description:
Anthropic’s initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to sources familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first time share sale ever.

The Claude AI model firm and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as US$64.4 billion (S$83 billion) in the IPO and US$26 billion in a private placement, its filings show.

Taken together, the offering would be bigger than SpaceX’s IPO, making it the biggest listing of all time.

Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers will be prioritised by Anthropic, and some would-be buyers will receive smaller allocations than they expect, some of the sources said.

Details of the IPO including the demand for shares could change, said the sources, who asked not to be identified as the information is not public.

A representative for Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The surge of interest in Anthropic shares contrasts with investors pulling back support for Nvidia Corp. after chief executive Jensen Huang was ousted from his post after reports of several affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China.

The chipmaker has agreed to buy about US$10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic as part of a US$26 billion private placement concurrent with its IPO, the artificial intelligence model firm’s filings show.

Anthropic counts Nvidia as a strategic partner, and has committed tens of billions of dollars to deals securing access to its most advanced chips.

Anthropic is looking to bolster demand for the IPO with a campaign of events for prospective investors, including a live-streamed event with its CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon on Nov 13, a source familiar with the matter has said.

The company is targeting a fully diluted valuation of about US$1.4 trillion, below where some investors expected the company to settle, Bloomberg News reported.

Some companies set terms conservatively when they begin formally marketing their IPO, in the expectation that strong demand will push up the final figure and set them up for robust trading in their debuts. 

Anthropic’s filing on Nov 10 supported the case for AI spending as sales continued to increase.

The company reported a revenue run rate of US$81 billion as at Oct 31, up US$10 billion from the end of September, the filing showed.

Anthropic had a US$65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported.

Anthropic defines the metric as annualising consumption-based fees for a trailing 28-day period and subscription-based fees for a single month.

Some investors are offering a portion of their Anthropic IPO allocation to other prospective backers, letting them collect additional fees and reduce their risk before trading begins, while others with pre-IPO stakes are marketing them to buyers via special purpose vehicles.

Goldman Sachs Group and Morgan Stanley are leading Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows.

The stock is expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Temasek to invest $342m in Godrej Industries’ financial services arm
data.description:
NEW DELHI – India’s Godrej Industries said on Nov 12 that Singapore’s Temasek Holdings will invest 25 billion rupees (S$342 million) in Godrej Capital through its affiliate, valuing the financial services business at up to 280 billion rupees.

Godrej Industries will retain about 80% ownership following the deal.

Temasek’s investment in Godrej Capital marks another bet on India’s financial services sector. Temasek also holds a stake in ICICI Bank, India’s second-largest private-sector bank by market capitalisation.

The deal adds to a series of large transactions in India’s financial services sector in 2026, including Fairfax Financial Holdings picking up a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank and Bank of America entering a joint venture to buy 49.9% stake in Jio Credit, the lending arm of Jio Financial Services.

“Financial services represents a major long-term growth area of focus for our Group, and our ambition is to build Godrej Capital into a 1 trillion-rupee AUM franchise by 2031,” said Pirojsha Godrej, chairman of Godrej Industries Group.

Founded in 2020, Godrej Capital operates in over 100 cities and had assets under management of 350 billion rupees as of Oct 31, 2026.

The company, through its subsidiaries, serves businesses and individuals across India with home loans, loans against property, working capital loans, construction finance and personal loans, among others.

The investment comes after Godrej Industries said it plans to list the financial services arm in the next five years. REUTERS

data.title: ST Engineering Q3 revenue rises 9% to $3.4 billion, declares interim dividend of 5 cents per share
data.description:
SINGAPORE – ST Engineering’s revenue for the third quarter ended September rose 9% year on year to $3.4 billion, from $3.1 billion in the previous corresponding period, the group said on Nov 13.

The technology and engineering company declared a third-quarter interim dividend of five cents per share, up from four cents a year earlier. Its first-quarter and second-quarter dividends were four cents and five cents per share, respectively, bringing the total for the first three quarters to 14 cents per share.

For the first nine months of 2026, revenue increased 10% to $10 billion, from $9.1 billion in the same period a year earlier. Excluding LeeBoy, its US-based construction equipment business divested on Sept 4, 2025, revenue grew 13% on a rebased basis.

Defence and public security was the group’s largest revenue contributor for the nine-month period, generating some $4.3 billion, up 7% year on year. Excluding LeeBoy, revenue from the segment grew 13%. Third-quarter revenue rose 8% to $1.4 billion, or 12% on a rebased basis.

The increase was led by marine and digital systems and cybersecurity businesses. The segment secured $5.5 billion in new contracts in the first nine months, including $1.8 billion in the third quarter. These included a five-year contract to supply 40mm ammunition to the British Ministry of Defence, projects involving defence command-and-control systems in Singapore, and maintenance and support services for the US Navy’s fleet.

Meanwhile, commercial aerospace revenue rose 12% to about $4.1 billion in the first nine months, supported by higher contributions from engine maintenance, repair and overhaul work and nacelles, a container for aircraft parts. Revenue for the third quarter increased 7% to $1.4 billion.

The segment secured $4.2 billion in new contracts in the first nine months, of which $1.4 billion was won in the third quarter. The latest wins included its first Airbus A220 airframe heavy maintenance contract with an Asia-Pacific operator and airframe maintenance agreements with Asia-Pacific airline customers.

Revenue from urban solutions and satellite communications increased 15% year on year to about $1.7 billion in the first nine months. Third-quarter revenue also rose 15% to $600 million, with higher contributions from both businesses.

The segment secured $3.5 billion in new contracts in the nine-month period, including $2.4 billion in the third quarter. Wins included turnkey rail services for the Taoyuan MRT Brown Line and Green Line Extension in Taiwan, integrated smart security management solutions contracts in Singapore and tolling infrastructure modernisation work for the Tampa-Hillsborough Expressway Authority in the US.

Across the group, contract wins totalled $13.2 billion in the first nine months, including $5.6 billion in the third quarter. The nine-month figure excluded $1.7 billion in New Jersey Turnpike Authority order book recognition.

The group’s order book stood at a record $37.7 billion as at September, up from $33.2 billion as at end-2025. About $3.1 billion is expected to be delivered in the remainder of 2026.

ST Engineering also reported a record-low operating expenses-to-revenue ratio of 9% for the first nine months, compared with 10.2% for the whole of 2025. The 2025 figure excluded a one-off impairment loss of iDirect group.

Nuclear energy

Separately, ST Engineering said it is exploring long-term opportunities in the nuclear energy sector, drawing on its capabilities in complex, safe and mission-critical environments and partnering organisations with complementary expertise.

Its current collaborations include those with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research, Sembcorp Utilities and Commonwealth Fusion Systems. Areas of activity include factory-fabricated structural modules, such as protective steel structures, and advanced materials for fusion reactors, including tungsten coatings for reactor’s inner walls.

The group also sees opportunities to apply its capabilities in digital twin technology and artificial intelligence, advanced materials and manufacturing, and large-scale systems integration.

Shares of ST Engineering were down 0.9% to close at $9.67 on Nov 13. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: ‘Renewed confidence’: Singtel lifts FY2027 guidance as underlying profit grows 10%, net profit falls 55%
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Telecommunications giant Singtel on Nov 13 raised financial year 2027 growth guidance for its operating companies’ (Opco) earnings before interest and taxes (Ebit) to between mid and high single digits.

This was an upgrade from the guidance of low- to mid-single-digit growth it gave in May, and the second year in a row that the telco has raised its Opco Ebit guidance at the half-year mark.

The revision came on the back of an 8.7% rise in first-half Opco Ebit to $902 million.

The growth was led by strong performance by Australian subsidiary Optus, tech service provider NCS and its digital infrastructure arm Digital InfraCo.

Optus’ Ebit rose 13.7% to A$322 million (S$282 million), NCS’ rose 15.5% to $212 million and Digital InfraCo’s rose 25.3% to $51 million.

Arthur Lang, group chief financial officer of Singtel, said at a media briefing of the company’s first-half results on Nov 13 that the telco was entering the second half of the year “with a renewed confidence versus six months ago”.

His comments came even as the telco reported a 54.7% drop in net profit to $1.5 billion for the first half ended September, in the absence of exceptional gains recorded the previous year. Underlying profit for the period was up 10.4% at $1.5 billion.

Lang said that when the group set its initial set of guidance in May, the Strait of Hormuz crisis had just broken out and inflation was a concern.

Moreover, the proposed merger of Simba and M1 had just been called off, adding a new degree of uncertainty.

In addition, Singtel said that it was also reviewing its capital expenditure guidance of about $3 billion.

The group expects capital expenditure to be lower than initially estimated on the back of disciplined capital allocation.

Singtel Singapore Ebit down

However, Singtel Singapore’s Ebit was down 4.5% as a result of the absence of one-off income recorded in the corresponding period the previous year.

Excluding the one-off, Singtel Singapore’s Ebit was down 1%.

Singapore mobile service revenue grew 3.8% in the second quarter from the first quarter, its second consecutive quarter of sequential growth.

Group chief executive Yuen Kuan Moon said this followed seven quarters of decline.

Average revenue per user rose to $23 for the quarter ended Sept 30, from $22 the previous quarter.

The telco attributed the rise to its three-brand strategy of Singtel, Gomo and hi!.

“We are not interested in going after just the pure volume of subscribers,” said Ng Tian Chong, CEO of Singtel Singapore.

Optus stake sale still on the table

In July, Singtel confirmed that it was in discussion with interested parties to sell a stake in Optus.

Yuen said Singtel’s search for a minority “like-minded Australian partner” for Optus was still ongoing.

However, given the strong performance of Optus, Lang noted that a stake in the company will not be available “at any value”.

Earlier media reports noted that New Zealand-based infrastructure investor Morrison was in talks to buy a minority stake valued at more than A$2 billion.

First-half earnings

Singtel said that its first-half financial year 2027 net profit decline was mainly due to the absence of $2.2 billion in net exceptional gains recorded a year earlier from the partial sale of its stake in Airtel and the Intouch-Gulf Energy merger.

Excluding exceptional items, underlying net profit rose about 10% from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

The group’s operating revenue rose 5.5% to $7.3 billion in the first half, from $6.9 billion in the year-ago period.

In constant currency terms, revenue would have increased 1.4%, while underlying net profit would have grown 15.9%, Singtel said.

The board approved an interim dividend of nine cents per share, comprising a core dividend of 7.1 cents and a value realisation dividend of 1.9 cents. This was 10% higher than the 8.2 cents per share declared a year earlier.

Shares of Singtel closed four cents or 1 per cent lower at $4.11 on Nov 13. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Global AI stocks sink as Nvidia CEO’s exit deepens sector sell-off
data.description:
Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Nov 12 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker’s leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said.

As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips – a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens.

Nvidia’s shares fell 8.2% to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion (S$5.14 trillion) for the first time since July 2025.

“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading.

Nvidia-backed neocloud firms CoreWeave dropped 9.1% after surging more than 27% in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks.

Other neocloud stocks including IREN and Applied Digital were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2% after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast.

Nvidia has lost about US$550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Nov 8 into Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.

“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility. We’re going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels,” said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

Nvidia short sellers have made US$9.6 billion in on-paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX.

AI sell-off continues after brief respite

Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the sell-off, with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3%.

Marvell Technology, which Huang called as the “next trillion-dollar company” in June, slumped 3.8%.

AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6%.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5% and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6% and 3.7%. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3% and 5.1%.

Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5% each.

Shares of AMD and Broadcom, which also produce AI chips and compete with Nvidia, however, rose 3.7% and 5.6%, respectively, on expectations that the turmoil at Nvidia could create opportunity for rivals.

Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8% and 2.7%.

AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier in November after the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centres, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out.

Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7% lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1%.

Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG. REUTERS

data.title: Megaspeed has hired a US law firm to review export control compliance, says Singaporean director
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Megaspeed International, the Singapore buyer of Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips that has come under global scrutiny, has engaged a US law firm to review its compliance with American export control laws.

In a Nov 12 statement issued by its Singaporean director Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, the company said the law firm would conduct a comprehensive inventory of its graphics processing units and independently verify its export control compliance practices.

Tan signed off as Megaspeed’s chairman and chief executive.

Previous attempts by The Straits Times to contact him were unsuccessful.

Tan said Megaspeed had also cooperated with inspections by the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees American export controls.

The company added that it was prepared to cooperate fully with other relevant US government authorities.

“Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously,” Tan said.

He added that compliance was a fundamental priority for the company, which was committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government.

The statement comes amid scrutiny of Megaspeed’s purchases of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which are subject to US export restrictions aimed at limiting China’s access to cutting-edge computing technology.

The Financial Times reported in November that the US authorities had considered placing Megaspeed on a trade blacklist over concerns about possible chip diversion, but a decision had been delayed.

Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said on Oct 31 that investigations into Megaspeed remained ongoing.

Megaspeed said it welcomed appropriate government scrutiny and was committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operated responsibly and in accordance with applicable US laws.

Megaspeed was previously known as 7Road International, a Chinese gaming company with ties to state-backed investors.

Huang Le, or Alice Huang – who was reported to have had an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang – joined the company as a director and managing director in March 2023, around the same time it was renamed.

She left Megaspeed on Nov 10, 2023, the same day Tan and another individual, Kang Kai, were appointed directors.

Kang left the board of the Singapore-registered company on Dec 28, 2023, but his name still appears in the corporate filings of Megaspeed’s overseas subsidiaries.

data.title: ‘I’ll be buying more’: Singapore investors pour into Nvidia shares on Jensen Huang’s exit
data.description:
SINGAPORE – When news broke of former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang being ensnared in an alleged honey trap espionage, retail investor Asiya Bakht was quick to snap up shares in the world’s biggest chip company.

“Nvidia shares had already been on a steep decline even before news of Huang’s resignation broke, so I was monitoring it closely… When the price dipped further following the announcement, I picked up a few more,” said the 52-year-old.

Her current Nvidia holding is already worth five figures, and she plans to plough more into the stock, having picked up shares throughout the week.

“I feel this temporary dip could be a major opportunity for investors like me,” said the founder of public relations company Beets PR.

She is among a wave of Singapore-based retail investors who rushed into Nvidia amid the sell-off on the night of Nov 12, betting that the company’s long-term growth prospects would outweigh the uncertainty surrounding its chief executive.

Trading activity surged in several brokerage platforms when US markets opened overnight, with investors largely buying the dip or holding on to their existing positions.

Nvidia shares had already been battered by a broader sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks, even before reports emerged over the weekend of Huang’s extramarital affairs.

But as the AI rout retraced some losses, Nvidia was hit by an alleged espionage accusation. Huang was reportedly involved with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of espionage.

The national security scandal was compounded by a governance issue when it was revealed that he also had an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice-president of its healthcare business.

With the chipmaker’s board under pressure to terminate his appointment, Huang resigned on Nov 12, sending Nvidia shares down another 14% by the opening of US trading, and down 4.3% at closing.

The Nov 12 close represents an 11% decline in Nvidia’s share price over the week, wiping about US$490 billion (S$630 billion) off the chipmaker’s market value over the period.

Buys placed ‘within minutes’

Despite the sharp sell-off, intrepid Singapore investors pounced on the buying opportunity on the night of Nov 12.

“Customers were placing buy orders within minutes of the price drop (when US market opened),” said Arpit Agal, head of brokerage at Syfe.

Nvidia orders on the platform surged to about 13 times the daily average over the preceding six weeks on the platform, following news of Huang’s resignation on Nov 12.

Of the clients who traded US stocks on Nov 12, 70% were dealing in Nvidia.

Similarly, FSM Global recorded a surge in Nvidia trading on Nov 12 night. Trading volume rose to 11 times its October daily average, with Singapore clients remaining net buyers of the counter at a buy-to-sell ratio of 1.35.

Over at brokerage firm IG, trading activity among Singapore peaked on Nov 12. Trading volume surged nearly six times over the past week compared with the preceding week, while the number of clients trading Nvidia roughly doubled.

The increase in activity was broad-based, spanning existing Nvidia shareholders, first-time traders of the stock and new IG clients.

“Investors are not necessarily losing faith in Nvidia’s business, but are reassessing the risks associated with iconic founder Jensen Huang’s departure,” said Jaycee Lai, head of clients at IG.

He added that client trading activity suggested that confidence in Nvidia’s underlying business remains relatively resilient.

Hedging bets

Singapore-based investors were already increasing their positions in Nvidia from earlier in the week, when news of Huang’s scandal broke out.

At FSM Global, Nvidia’s buy-to-sell ratio among Singapore clients touched 3.3 on Nov 9, compared with 1.1 in October.

Saxo also reported that Singapore clients remained slightly tilted towards buying, with the number of clients holding Nvidia positions increasing around 3% on Nov 12.

However, unlike the spree on that day, investors appeared more cautious earlier in the week as the controversy unfolded.

While Moomoo Singapore recorded a near three-times increase in Nvidia sell orders and shares sold between Nov 6 and 9, put option contracts rose by more than five times.

Despite the increase in selling activity, clients remained net buyers on both days. Moomoo noted that the broader technology sell-off and the usual pickup in Monday trading likely contributed to the rise in activity.

At Syfe, call options also outweighed puts by around nine to one in value, although the proportion of put orders increased from 44% to 47% this week.

This suggested that some investors were hedging their positions, even as overall sentiment remained optimistic, said Agal at Syfe.

Spillover into other technology counters appeared limited at IG and Saxo, although FSM Global observed increased net buying in Nvidia rivals AMD and Broadcom.

Focus shifts to Nvidia’s leadership

With Huang’s departure, investors are now turning their attention to Nvidia’s leadership and governance, particularly the implications for its long-term strategy.

Nvidia has appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive while it searches for a permanent replacement.

Huang’s central role in Nvidia’s technology direction, product strategy and customer relationships makes any leadership transition a tough challenge, said You Weiren, senior portfolio manager at FSM Global.

Nevertheless, he remained positive on Nvidia’s fundamentals, citing continued AI demand.

However, he warned that further volatility could emerge around its earnings announcement on Nov 17, and a congressional briefing scheduled for Nov 18.

Not all investors have thrown caution to the wind.

Marc Low, a product manager at a financial-services company, has yet to make any trades on the counter this week.

The 43-year-old is waiting to see how the company navigates the “power vacuum”, as it searches for a suitable successor to Huang.

For others such as Joel Tan, Huang’s departure from Nvidia spells the death knell for its share price. The 29-year-old banker intends to sell his holdings.

“Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia has grown into a trillion-dollar company and delivered strong stock performance. It would be difficult to replace that kind of track record.” THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Long John Silver’s White Sands outlet to shutter on Nov 18
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Fast-food chain Long John Silver’s will be closing its restaurant at White Sands shopping mall in Pasir Ris on Nov 18.

According to a notice pasted outside the outlet, its last day of operations is Nov 17.

A homemaker, who wanted to be known only as Afifah, said she often takes her children to the White Sands outlet for meals after school.

“I’m sad that there will be one fewer halal meal option after this place closes. My children like the food here,” said the 40-year-old, who was having lunch there.

Another diner, human resources executive Benjamin Lee, who works in the area, said he sometimes patronises the White Sands outlet during his lunch hour.

“I don’t feel much about the outlet closing as there are always other lunch options around,” said the 38-year-old.

“But it seems like a lot of food and beverage outlets have been closing in 2026, so that’s a pity.”

The impending outlet closure marks the latest of several in 2026 for the fast-food chain known for its golden battered seafood. Its Woodlands outlet was permanently shuttered on Oct 31.

Long John Silver’s Singapore website now lists 10 outlets, including White Sands. This is down from the 17 outlets reported by the media in July 2025.

Its Jurong Point outlet shut on Oct 19, and checks show that at least four other locations closed earlier in 2026.

Based on social media posts as well as media reports, those affected outlets were in Suntec City, Admiralty, Commonwealth and Tampines.

Long John Silver’s traces its roots in Singapore back to the 1980s, as part of the wave of US fast-food chains that entered the local market.

Today, its outlets here are all managed by Zensho Food Singapore, a subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate Zensho Holdings Group, which is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

The parent group manages a global portfolio of popular F&B brands, including Japan’s leading beef bowl restaurant chain Sukiya and Ichikokudo Hokkaido Ramen, which both have a presence in Singapore.

The Straits Times has contacted Zensho Food Singapore for more information.

data.title: Taiwan’s Foxconn bullish on outlook but warns about supply chain tightness
data.description:
TAIPEI – Taiwan’s Foxconn, the world’s largest contract electronics maker, said on Nov 12 it was confident about its business in 2027 given strong AI demand as it reported forecast-beating quarterly profit, but it warned about supply chain tightness.

Net profit for the July to September period for Nvidia’s biggest server maker and Apple’s top iPhone assembler was NT$77.5 billion (S$3.02 billion), up 34% on year and beating an LSEG consensus estimate of NT$69.6 billion.

In an earnings release, Foxconn stuck to its previous forecast of “strong” growth for revenue in 2026 and said it saw strong AI demand throughout 2026 and into 2027.

The company, which does not give numeric forecasts, said it predicted “high double digit growth” in 2027 for AI rack shipments.

“We remain very confident about our operations next year and expect continued growth,” chairman Young Liu told an earnings conference, although warning there were also “several external variables worth continued attention”.

Looking at the AI and consumer electronics supply chains, chips, memory and some key components are currently tight, which is a challenge facing the industry as a whole, Liu said.

“Although supply bottlenecks should gradually ease as new capacity comes online, overall demand is expected to still exceed supply next year, and the tight supply-demand situation may persist for some time,” he said.

Foxconn, formally called Hon Hai Precision Industry, in October reported a 47% year-on-year jump in third-quarter revenue.

Most of the iPhones Foxconn makes for Apple are assembled in China, but it now produces the bulk of those sold in the United States in India. The company is also building factories in Mexico and Texas to make AI servers for Nvidia.

Foxconn has been looking to expand its footprint in electric vehicles as well.

The company’s shares have risen 4% so far in 2026, underperforming a 49% gain on the broader Taiwan index.

Foxconn shares closed 0.8% lower on Nov 12 ahead of the earnings release. The main index ended down 2.6%. REUTERS

data.title: Alphabet raises almost US$4 billion from Hong Kong, Singapore bond sales
data.description:
HONG KONG – Alphabet raised almost US$4 billion (S$5 billion) in equivalent funds in Asia through inaugural Hong Kong- and Singapore-dollar bond sales, testing investor appetite at a time of increasing volatility for companies focused on artificial intelligence.

The Google parent sold a three-part Hong Kong dollar bond, consisting of two-year, five-year and 10-year tranches, for a total of HK$16 billion (S$2.6 billion), and a four-part Singapore dollar bond, consisting of two-year, five-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches, for S$2.28 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The Hong Kong dollar-denominated bonds tightened by 25 to 30 basis points from initial thoughts, while the Singapore dollar notes priced at 20 to 25 basis points tighter than initially indicated, said the person, who asked not to be identified discussing non-public information.

Orders for the Hong Kong dollar tranches exceeded HK$32.5 billion by the time final guidance was released, while demand for the Singapore dollar tranches topped S$4 billion at that stage, according to the person.

“Asia’s local currency market is less crowded compared to the dollar market,” said Gary Ng, senior economist at Natixis.

“Deals such as Alphabet’s offer local investors a rare combination of highly rated global technology company and debt in their own currencies, which should attract strong demand,” he said.

Proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, which may include the repayment of outstanding debt.

The deal comes at a challenging moment for technology industry borrowers.

Investors have become more cautious toward AI-linked assets after a broad market selloff last week fuelled by concerns that a Democrat sweep in the US midterm elections could lead to greater scrutiny of data centre development and AI infrastructure spending.

The sector has also been shaken by market turmoil sparked by Nvidia, the leading maker of AI chips, which has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive Jensen Huang.

Alphabet’s fund-raising effort is part of a broader push by global hyperscalers to tap new debt markets as they seek financing for AI-related projects.

The company sold its first Australian dollar bonds in August and has also issued notes in Swiss francs, British pounds, Canadian dollars and Japanese yen in 2026.

Alphabet and other firms, including Microsoft, Amazon.com and Meta Platforms, have been borrowing at a record pace while simultaneously committing tens of billions of dollars to build out AI capabilities.

Earlier in November, Alphabet raised €6 billion (S$8.5 billion) through a multi-tranche euro bond sale, its second offering in the currency in 2026.

The company paid materially higher borrowing costs than in its inaugural euro deal in May as concerns over the pace of AI spending rose. BLOOMBERG

data.title: US firm Advent seeks to sell Singapore tutor chain Learning Lab again, sources say
data.description:
SINGAPORE – US buyout firm Advent International has put up Singapore’s tutor-chain The Learning Lab for sale, marking its second attempt since 2021 to unload the asset, in part to repay debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

Advent has hired an adviser to kick-start the sale process and plans to offer the company for about US$400 million to US$500 million (S$514.6 million to S$643.3 million), said the people who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. Some of the proceeds will be used to settle a S$265 million private credit facility jointly provided by KKR & Co, HPS Investment Partners and Nomura Holdings in 2023 and which will mature in 2027, they said.

Representatives for Advent, KKR and Nomura declined to comment. HPS did not respond to a request for comment.

Private money has been pouring into schools in Asia in recent years as investors seek to profit from growing demand for quality education. Financiers such as Apollo Global Management and KKR have bought stakes and lent to school chains, hoping that a growing number of rich people in the region would fuel expansion.

But private equity and venture capital investment in education services in Asia slumped 87% to US$240 million in 2025, according to S&P Global, citing more rigorous deal selection and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on the sector. Another key challenge is the backlog of private equity firms seeking to exit companies they have bought into.

Advent invested in The Learning Lab in 2014, but there has been no publicly available information on how much stake it holds. People with knowledge of the matter said Advent fully owns the learning company.

The Learning Lab provides education for pre-school, primary, secondary and junior college students in Singapore, according to its website. It also has online services for other Asian markets including Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia. In Singapore, the company charges about S$702 a month for its junior college programmes. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Stocks recover from Nvidia whiplash, dollar climbs with US yields
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Stocks in Asia were on steadier footing on Nov 13 after a turbulent week dominated by revelations of extramarital affairs involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang that culminated in his resignation, in a blow to the global AI boom he helped advance.

US Treasury yields climbed, with the two-year yield hitting a one-month high, lifting the dollar as investors weighed the prospect of an outsized 50 basis point rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in December.

Huang stepped down on Nov 12 after reports of the affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, which plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves through the AI industry.

His exit could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader artificial intelligence industry and supply chain, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump.

“His departure leaves a vacuum that will be difficult to fill... We do not assume existing commitments change, but new deals could take longer or require more compensation as investors look for reassurance about Nvidia’s role,” analysts at JPMorgan said in a note.

“The bigger implications are for the rest of the AI trade, particularly GPU (graphics processing unit) financing and infrastructure deals in which Nvidia would presumably be involved as a supplier, investor or provider of contractual support.”

Nvidia shares fell 3% in extended trading, while those of its customers, including South Korea’s Naver, extended declines on Nov 13, with Naver down 2.75%.

Jon Zauderer, Citi’s head of specialist sales, said competitors such as AMD, Arista and Broadcom could benefit from the Nvidia fallout.

“If you think about the uncertainty that’s created about a potential management change, investors are going to look for alternatives,” he said.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 0.26%, reversing some of its 1.3% fall from the previous session.

South Korea’s Kospi rose 2.35%, while Japan’s Nikkei added 1.4%.

The recovery in global equities also follows last week’s market meltdown sparked by US Republicans’ electoral drubbing, which stoked fears that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure build-out that has helped send stocks to record highs in 2026.

Nasdaq futures and S&P 500 futures rose more than 0.2% each, while EURO STOXX 50 futures fell 0.37%.

US Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott sent letters on Nov 12 to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Huang, asking them to testify over the recent developments at Nvidia.

Concerns over the AI outlook also spilt into metals, with London copper prices hitting a four-month low in the previous session on fears of weaker demand, while shares of Australian-listed miner Capstone Copper Corp fell more than 5% on Nov 13.

What will the Fed do?

The two-year US Treasury yield peaked at 4.8920% in the early Asian session, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose to a three-week high of 5.1433%.

Investors now see a 14.5% chance of a jumbo 50-basis-point Fed hike in December, up from zero a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

“Right now, the US Fed has three hikes priced in for effectively the next 12 months... The (most recent) CPI (consumer price index) print obviously was a bit hotter than expected. If those kinds of prints continue to happen, we can definitely see the Fed hiking three more times. It’s very within the realms of possibility,” said Manusha Samaraweera, fixed income investment director at Capital Group.

The increasingly hawkish Fed expectations in turn boosted the dollar, which was on track for a weekly gain of 0.9%, its biggest in more than a month.

The strength in the greenback, meanwhile, weighed on the yen, which languished close to the key 160 per dollar level on Nov 13, leaving traders on alert for any intervention from Tokyo.

The Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Nov 12 it bought 79.4 billion yen (S$638.9 million) in the spot market on July 31, selling euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund as part of a joint US-Japan intervention this summer to shore up the yen.

Elsewhere, Brent crude futures and US crude fell more than 0.3% each to US$95.45 and US$88.39 a barrel, respectively, having jumped in the previous session after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated and shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz threatened global oil flows.

Spot gold was up 0.3% at US$3,888.01 an ounce. REUTERS

data.title: No love for Lambo: Luxury car dealer EuroSports reports losses, seeks funding to support business
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Singapore’s Lamborghini dealer EuroSports Global is looking to new luxury models to draw buyers after a tough quarter of falling sales, even as it seeks fresh funding to support its car business and plans to mass-produce a home-grown electric motorcycle.

The group on Nov 12 said its net loss had widened to $1.24 million in the quarter ended Sept 30, from $752,000 a year earlier. Revenue fell by more than 30% to $7.83 million.

For the first half of its financial year, the group’s net loss widened by 57% to $2.29 million as revenue fell 21.7% to $15.1 million, weighed down by falling car sales and thinner margins on cars sold.

EuroSports is the distributor for Lamborghini and Touring Superleggera in Singapore, with some models selling for more than $2 million.

However, hefty additional registration fees for luxury vehicles and rising certificate of entitlement premiums have crimped demand for high-end supercars here. EuroSports also expects economic and geopolitical uncertainty to make buyers more cautious in the months ahead.

But the group said new models could help attract more orders, and expects to start delivering two new versions of Lamborghini’s Urus SE sport utility vehicle in the October-to-December quarter, although prices for this model may be lower.

Lamborghini is also expected to introduce a new version of its Temerario sports car by March 2027, following the recent launch of its Revuelto SV.

EuroSports’ electric motorcycle business has a longer timeline. The Lambda Scorpii, developed by its subsidiary Scorpio Electric, became the first electric motorcycle designed from scratch in Singapore to secure European vehicle-type approval in 2025, the group said.

The approval certifies that the motorcycle meets European Union safety, environmental and technical standards.

The motorcycle secured approval from Singapore’s Land Transport Authority on June 12, and Scorpio Electric registered the first unit for use on Singapore roads on July 13.

It is also setting up sales and servicing networks in the Asia-Pacific and Europe, with plans to build a network of distributors and dealers across 10 to 15 cities.

EuroSports expects mass production and deliveries to begin in 2028, and is in the process of securing additional funding to support the commercialisation of this business.

The company has spent heavily on research and development for the Lambda Scorpii, which has placed pressure on its financials over the years.

The group disclosed in its financial statements that its losses, cash outflow and short-term obligations raised a material uncertainty over its ability to continue operating. In the first half, it burned through $1.18 million in cash to run its operations.

As at Sept 30, what it owed in the short term exceeded its short-term assets – which included cash, cars and spare parts held for sale, and money that customers owe the company – by $6.54 million.

Still, the board said it expects the car distribution business to generate enough cash to cover operating expenses over the next 12 months. It is in talks with financial institutions and potential investors for additional funding to support operations over at least that period.

Shares of the company last traded at 2.4 cents.

data.title: Alibaba-Megaspeed financing link traced via S’pore, Malaysia units amid Nvidia chip scrutiny
data.description:
SINGAPORE – A Singapore company owned by Chinese tech giant Alibaba had a financial arrangement with the Malaysian subsidiary of Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia chip buyer under scrutiny over the possible diversion of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China.

Corporate records obtained by The Straits Times show that Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, pledged specified IT and network equipment, intellectual property and related rights to Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) under an agreement dated June 18, 2024. The arrangement gave Apex security over the assets should Speedmatrix fail to meet certain contractual obligations.

Malaysian corporate records show that the arrangement remained active as at Nov 11, 2026.

The financial connection was highlighted in a May report by US short-seller Culper Research, which alleged that Alibaba may have channelled billions of dollars through Apex to finance Megaspeed’s purchases of Nvidia chips.

The research firm, which had taken a position that would benefit from the fall of Nvidia’s share price, suggested that Alibaba had provided the funds to Apex, which may have passed a substantial portion to Megaspeed for distribution to its overseas subsidiaries.

Apex was incorporated in Singapore in July 2023 and it is registered at Lazada One in Bras Basah Road, which is leased by Alibaba and its South-east Asian online shopping unit, Lazada Group.

Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority records show that Apex’s immediate holding company is Cloud Intelligence (Cayman) Holding.

Its ultimate holding company is Alibaba Group Holding, which is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and has contractual rights to Alibaba China’s profits.

Apex, in its audited financial statement for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, described its business activity as “providing procurement activities”.

Its corporate records also showed that Yuan Qian served as a director from August 2023 to August 2025.

The name matches the Chinese name of Selina Yuan, a former Alibaba executive who has headed Alibaba Cloud’s international business in Singapore, but ST has not independently confirmed that she is the director named in Apex’s records.

Apex’s current directors are Gong Zhengyuan, Zhu Bofu and Madelyn Kwang Yeit Lam, a Singaporean who also serves as the company secretary.

Kwang has also been listed as a director and secretary of Alibaba Cloud (Singapore) since 2016. She did not respond to ST’s queries.

Apex’s auditor is PwC. When contacted, a spokesperson said: “This relates to a client matter, we are therefore unable to comment.”

The Financial Times reported in November that Alibaba was one of Megaspeed’s major customers for its South-east Asian cloud service operation.

Alibaba and Megaspeed did not respond to ST’s queries on the nature of their commercial relationships and whether the relationships have remained intact with investigations into Megaspeed.

Megaspeed’s overseas network

Megaspeed owns seven subsidiaries across five overseas markets, according to its financial statements for 2024, which are its latest publicly available records.

Three are in Malaysia: Speedmatrix, Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd and MSFusion. All three are private limited companies.

Speedmatrix and Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd were described as cloud-hosting service providers. MSFusion was classified as dormant at end-2024, but it entered a RM263.2 million (S$82.8 million) agreement to buy a site in Johor for a proposed data centre, according to the seller’s bourse filing in August 2025.

Megaspeed also owned 99.99% of Megaspeed (Thailand) and 99% of PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, both cloud-hosting businesses.

The other two Megaspeed’s wholly owned subsidiaries are in Australia and the US.

Megaspeed’s latest shipment recorded on corporate intelligence platform Sayari was to Speedmatrix – an Nvidia baseboard for high-performance graphics processing units, which arrived on Nov 18, 2025.

The top receivers of Megaspeed’s shipments were Speedmatrix and PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, according to Sayari.

Official scrutiny

Megaspeed has attracted international attention because of its massive purchases of Nvidia’s advanced AI chips, some of which are subject to US export restrictions intended to limit China’s access to powerful computing technology.

The US authorities began investigating Megaspeed over suspicions that it breached US chip export restrictions in late 2024.

The Singapore police confirmed in October 2025 that they were investigating Megaspeed over “suspected breaches of our domestic laws”.

The firm drew more scrutiny in late October 2026, when news broke that the US was concerned about Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s close ties to Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, Megaspeed’s former director and managing director.

On Nov 8, Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair. He resigned on Nov 12.

Access to Megaspeed’s office at Ocean Financial Centre is restricted. It showed no signs of activity when ST visited the office in October 2025. A tenant then told ST the office was empty “for as long as it has been” there.

On Nov 11, ST visited the registered address of Swiftdata, the little-known Singapore company that owns Megaspeed, and found it seemingly occupied by an interior design firm, whose co-founder denied knowing Swiftdata, Megaspeed or any of their affiliates.

ST was unable to contact Swiftdata or its sole director Tan Yong Pong, who was appointed Megaspeed’s director in 2023 on the day Alice Huang left the board.

A statement on Megaspeed’s website posted on Nov 12 said it has engaged a US law firm to “lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units and independently verify its export control compliance practices”.

The statement was attributed to Tan, who signed off as the company’s chairman and chief executive.

data.title: New business-class seats, Air India plans among key takeaways from SIA’s first-half results briefing
data.description:
SINGAPORE – A week after receiving mixed feedback on its newly unveiled business-class seats, Singapore Airlines chief executive Goh Choon Phong said the airline would explore the possibility of making adjustments where it deemed fit.

Without elaborating on the extent of any possible changes, Goh said at SIA’s results briefing on Nov 12 that the group acknowledges the feedback it had received and would review it so that it could “further enhance” the travel experience for its customers.

SIA also elaborated on the growth strategy for loss-making Air India, in which it holds a 25.1% stake, noting that the airline is aiming to achieve profitability under new leadership and with growth opportunities emerging in the market.

The company posted $5.6 billion in revenue, 14.3% higher year on year, for the second quarter ended Sept 30. Net profit also quadrupled to $209.7 million.

Despite the strong quarter, the airline’s net profit for the first half of its financial year still fell 43.9% to $134 million, as rising jet fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict took a toll on its performance.

Jet fuel prices were lower in the second quarter than the first quarter, said group chief financial officer JoAnn Tan.

The surge, however, still led to a 90.3% increase in fuel costs before hedging for the first half of the financial year.

Shares of SIA closed Nov 12 at $7.25, up 1.1%.

Here are the key takeaways from SIA’s results briefing for the first half of its 2027 financial year:

Possible changes to the business-class seat

SIA’s long-haul business-class seats, revealed on Nov 7 alongside refreshed products across all its other cabin classes, has sparked substantial debate.

Central to the discussion were the seat’s shape and grey palette, which drew comparisons to a dental chair, and the bright yellow stripe across the backrest, which critics said strayed too far from the colours traditionally associated with the airline.

The business-class cabin was designed by BMW Group’s Designworks, one of three design studios hired by SIA to design its fleetwide overhaul for $2 billion in total.

Due to launch in the second half of 2027, the seats will be introduced progressively on 41 Airbus A350-900 long-haul and ultra-long-range aircraft as they are retrofitted, as well as on SIA’s upcoming Boeing 777-9 planes. Deliveries of the Boeing aircraft have already been delayed by five years, and the model is still awaiting certification.

SIA has defended the seat’s design following the public outcry and now says it will consider adjustments in response to feedback. A petition on Change.org is calling for the airline to remove the yellow accents.

Asked by The Straits Times whether engaging a single agency for the entire redesign could have produced a more unified look and reduced costs, Goh said the airline’s decision was based on the different requirements of each cabin class.

“What we’ve done is to choose the most appropriate agency for the needs of that specific business class,” he said.
